articleTitle: Device for monitoring people with Alzheimer's disease
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This paper presents the method used for designing, constructing, and assembling a device that is used for monitoring health parameters for Alzheimer suffering patients. By using one sensor for environmental temperature, atmospheric pressure and for heart pulse, it displays all those parameters on a little display, and also on a smartphone via Bluetooth connection.

articleTitle: Convolution Kernel Size Effect on Convolutional Neural Network in Histopathological Image Processing Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In this study, the change in the classification success of the convolutional neural network (CNN) is investigated when the dimensions of the convolution window are altered. For this purpose, four different linear convolution neural network architectures are constructed. The first architecture includes 4 convolution layers with 3×3 convolution window dimensions. The second architecture includes 4 convolution layers with 5×5 convolution window dimensions. The third architecture includes 4 convolution layers with 7×7 convolution window dimensions. The fourth architecture includes 4 convolution layers with 9×9 convolution window dimensions. A dataset consisting of histopathological image patches is used to test the CNN architects that are created. 2000 training images and 250 validation images on dataset are applied to all architectures with the same order, in order to fair assessment. In conclusion, the effect of convolution dimensions on classification of histopathological images by deep learning methods is determined. The test results of four different linear convolutional neural network architectures are evaluated using sensitivity, specificity and accuracy parameters.

articleTitle: Frequency Domain Models for Nonlinear Home Appliance Devices
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: New frequency domain models for nonlinear home appliances as air conditioning systems, vacuum cleaners, microwave ovens and compact fluorescent lamps are proposed. These models employ measured amplitudes and phases of the current fundamental and harmonic components. The harmonic balance simulation using these models is very fast.

articleTitle: Simulation and Design of Thin-Film Thermoelectric Generators
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Design of thin-film thermoelectric generators for low power applications, for example, for power sources of human monitoring systems, has been considered in the paper. The obtained output power is from 3 μW to 56 μW and the temperature differences from 25K to 100K. The design has been based on simulation methodology proposed by the authors. The simulations have been done by finite element method using ANSYS.

articleTitle: A Smart Residential Microgrid Based on Renewable Energy Sources with Integrated Electric Vehicle Charging Station
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The projected growth of electric vehicles (EVs) in the near future, especially in cities, will have a dramatic effect on the power consumption profile. The power grids are expected to become overloaded due to the EV charging taking place at peak periods of the day. To address this issue, the paper proposes a smart microgrid solution based on renewable energy sources installed on the premises of a residential consumer. The MG also includes an EV charging station available for external users in exchange for a fee. The paper presents the practical implementation of the system based on commercially available equipment, which makes it more economically and technically feasible. The principles behind the proposed control system are also depicted.

articleTitle: Flicker Free Visible Light Communication Using Low Frame Rate Camera
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Over the years, more and more conventional lighting systems tend to be replaced by LED lighting systems because of their advantages such as high energy efficiency, longer lifespan and lower heat generation. Because of the LEDs' capability of switching to different light intensities at fast rate, these lighting solutions could be used for both illumination and transferring data. This characteristic of the LEDs has led to the development of a new technology, known as Visible Light Communication (VLC). In this type of communication, the receiver is usually a photodetector. Lately, the tendency is to also use video cameras to receive the transmitted data. Solutions exist, but they use expensive cameras that can capture over 800 frames per second (fps). The communication proposed in the paper uses a LED as a transmitter and a camera with a common frame rate (120 fps) as the receiver. At those frame rates the challenge is to use a code that avoids flickering and does not need a synchronization between the transmitter and the receiver. A version for such code is also presented in the paper. The system was implemented and tested. The results confirm the functioning of the proposed low frame rate VLC communication system.

articleTitle: Passive RFID Tags for Textile Items – Requirements and Solutions
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Nowadays, new researches are developed for obtaining the smart labels attached to wearable and washable issues, taking into account the complex stresses to which these objects are subjected throughout their life cycle, from manufacturing, wearing and repeated washings to recycling. The distinctive category of smart labels - RFID tags accompanying textile issues must cover several requirements; in particular, they should have a longer life span than the targeted objects. This paper analyses the requirements imposed for conductive and dielectric materials used within the structure of the passive RFID tags, designed to identify and monitor textile articles. Through a properly selection of the materials and an appropriate structure for the transponder, a new type of passive UHF RFID tag is developed. The developed RFID passive tag has been tested with good results in the aggressive environment of industrial laundries, which confirms its good reliability and accuracy.

articleTitle: A Two-Stage Optimization Approach to Suppression of Side Lobe and Sideband Levels in Time-Modulated Linear Arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Time modulated arrays (TMA) suffer from relatively low efficiencies due to radiations at different harmonics (sidebands) of modulation frequency in addition to main frequency. In order to increase this efficiency, optimization algorithms are usually used, but the performance and solution time of the optimizations must be studied. In this study, the two-stage optimization method is proposed for suppressing sidelobe level (SLL) and switching-induced sideband levels (SBL) in the time-modulated linear antenna array. It is shown through a sample scenario that the proposed method gives more effective results than the classical optimization approach.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Capacitive Couplers in Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The capacitive power transfer (CPT) technology is mainly used in battery charging systems. The capacitive coupler plays a critical role in a CPT system. The capacitive coupler can be classified into two sections, unipolar and bipolar. The bipolar includes row and column couplers. This paper aims to analyse and compare the capacitive couplers. The plates dimension, plates spacing, and misalignment characteristics were analysed for each coupler. These parameters were considered as criteria to evaluate and compare the capacitive couplers in terms of investigation their effects on the coupling capacitance (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>). All couplers were examined in a CPT system with a dual LCL compensation circuit topology. The voltage stress of the components, power density, electric field emissions, and safety distance were evaluated. The results showed that the most components in a CPT system of a unipolar coupler have the highest voltage stress among other couplers. This indicates that the CPT system with the unipolar coupler requires passive components with high VA ratings, and high insulation requirements are necessary. Likewise, it was found that the highest power density and lowest safety distance among the other couplers were achieved by the unipolar and column couplers, respectively.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of 32-bit RISC-V Processor with Web-Based Assembler-Disassembler
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In this study, a pure structural implementation based, 32-bit open source RISC-V processor is presented. The proposed processor is designed using Verilog and it is implemented on Cyclone IV 4CE115 FPGA device available on Altera DE2-115 Board. Additionally, web-based assembler and disassembler tools are developed and published as a part of this project. Before using the target RISC-V processor, the user can generate machine code using the web-based assembler tool. Then, the generated machine code can be downloaded onto the RISC-V processor using UART. The web-based assembler and disassembler tools are developed with technologies such as HTML5, CSS and JavaScript. The proposed processor is a fully functional processor that uses RV32I base integer instructional set with 37 instructions. The amount of hardware resources used by the whole processor circuit is about 43.7% of the Cyclone IV 4CE115 FPGA device and the maximum frequency achieved for the processor is 150MHz without using any timing constraint.

articleTitle: Electric grid monitoring and control architecture for industry 4.0 systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The existing papers, technologies and products make possible the implementation of large-scale integrated systems that allow monitoring and control of an electric grid. Such a system presents several major advantages, like the ability to closer match the production and consumption of electricity in real time, realistically adjust the dimensions of infrastructure based on measured power requirements, pin-point problems in the grid etc. Furthermore, this system can be adapted and integrated into industry 4.0 systems, to provide control and visibility of the enterprise operations at low level. Nowadays, most of the tools and equipment use electric energy as the main power source or for control, while renewable energy production capabilities are installed in factories. This article presents the requirements for smart metering in an industry 4.0 system along with a proposed architecture for the private grid monitoring and control system. In our experiment, we adapt and integrate the latest transmission encryption methodologies over a wired network to ensure data security in an industrial environment. We bring contributions to the presentation layer in order to display the data in a simple to understand and meaningful way.

articleTitle: Water and Heat Exposure Influence on Dielectric Response of LDPE-Al2O3 Nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The influence of water and heat exposure on the dielectric response of LDPE-Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> nanocomposites with 2wt% filler content was analyzed in this paper. The dielectric spectra of the real and imaginary permittivities, over a frequency range of 10 mHz - 1 MHz and for temperatures from 30 to 70°C, measured before any exposure, after one week immersion in deionized water and after one week thermal aging at 90°C are presented and discussed in this paper, analyzing the stability of the dielectric properties to the applied stresses.

articleTitle: Smart Metering based Approaches to Solve the Load Phase Balancing Problem in Low Voltage Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Energy savings represent an important issue both for Distribution Networks Operators (DNOs) and final consumers. For each DNOs, while efficiency can be achieved by replacing old with newer devices, or by updating into the existing configuration another equipment. One of these problems can be solved using the Phase Load Balancing (PLB). This paper proposes a particular approach regarding the aforementioned problem. Then, the PLB problem was solved with the help of two approaches based on the heuristic and PSO algorithms, which use the data provided by Smart Meters. Both algorithms for PLB optimization problem were tested on a real low voltage (LV) electricity distribution network (EDN), and the results, quantified in electricity savings though loss reduction, proving their efficiency.

articleTitle: A New Approach for Harmonic Power Calculation of Nonuniform Time Modulated Arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In this work, a new idea about the sideband radiation (SR) of nonuniform time modulated Arrays (NTMA) is introduced. The calculations of the uniform systems have been studied in the literature and it is suggested that the same equations are valid for the nonuniform systems too. However, the idea that calculations should be different has been the main motivation source for this study. In order to simplify the system and obtain the calculation simplicity, a prime coefficient distribution is suggested and the power equation is derived from the fundamental equations. As a result, it is concluded that the solution of the nonuniform systems is different from the uniform one and the general opinion in the literature should be reviewed.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Control Strategy for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In this study is proposed a Simple Adaptive Control (SAC) design for a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (PMSM). The control system is constructed in rotor reference frame and forms a cascade structure. In the inner loop are controlled the direct and the quadrature currents and in the outer loop is controlled the angular speed of the shaft. The non-linear behaviour is compensated through feedforward controllers while an Extened Kalman Filter (EKF) is used to compensate unknown disturbances caused, for example, by deviations of parameters or by unconsidered dynamics. Thus, these compensations lead to a linear behaviour of the process over which the SAC strategy is overlapped. The performance of the adaptive control system is verified by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Synchronous Reluctance Machine modeling for accurate performances evaluation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The article gives an overview on different SynRM flux linkage and inductances estimation methods and assumptions in order to integrate nonlinear behavior of the machine, as well as the saturation and cross-saturation integration in the SynRM model. Analytical approach, Magnetic Equivalent Circuit and Finite Element analysis are used for magnetizing inductances and flux linkage computation, for two SynRM topologies.

articleTitle: Power quality analysis based on a novel nonlinear dependence between parameters of nonsinusoidal regime
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Power quality analysis is one of the most important subjects of every power systems' interconnected parts. In fact, the nonsinusoidal regime represents the real operation mode of all the power systems, due mainly to distribution and consumers. Several parameters of power quality analysis are used by every national power system operator to impose specific standard limits and regulation which ensure optimal conditions of the electrical energy quality. Generally, all the limit values must be respected, even though they indirectly depend on one another. This paper proposes new relations between some parameters of power quality for the case of most common linear and inductive consumers, in order to unify the limits imposed on nonsinusoidal regime. Starting by the definition of relative values of voltage and current harmonics a new nonlinear dependence between the power factor and the total harmonic distortion of voltage and current is established. A quantitative approach of the nonlinear function has been assessed by using Matlab tools. The results are compared and discussed to the measured data for a large industrial consumer in two cases: with and without filters for power factor correction.

articleTitle: An Efficient Solution for Video Compression Using an Original Modified Algorithm Applied to Improve the 3D Discrete Cosine Transform
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The 3D-DCT is used in video compression when the applied basic principle is the correlation between adjacent pixels in a frame and the correlation between pixels from the same position in adjacent frames (temporal correlation). This principle uses the concept that a video sequence can be seen as a parallelepiped representing the entire video sequence, divided into smaller, independently encoded parallelepipeds, the most commonly format being a "video cube" of 8×8×8 size. When passing this cube through the 3D-DCT algorithm that applies to it, the corresponding quantization tables must be known by both the encoder and the decoder to be able to decompress the video information. This paper presents an original method of implementing a modified 3D-DCT compression algorithm, which is a variant derived from it and which brings certain improvements to the standard algorithm. The main improvement is to replace fixed-sized "video cubes" by creating variable-length parallelepipeds over time, giving up the fixed value of 8 for the "video cube" dimension, which means considerable reductions in the volume of this parallelepiped when its sides are smaller than 8. n-bit operations can be performed more efficiently and resource-saving when n <; 8 and implicitly the value of 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> - 1 no longer complies with the divisibility by 8. Other improvements are related to how the information bits are saved when storing them in the compressed video file. Reading from this file and writing in this file run in large blocks, to avoid accessing the file too often with short readings or writings. The design and implementation details, as well as the analysis of the compression performance obtained (including the consumption of time divided by type of function used) are thoroughly presented in the paper.

articleTitle: IoT and Energy Efficiency for Smart Agriculture using Adcon Telemetry Devices
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The IoT concept has grown in recent years and has transformed people’s lives by making them easier, regardless of the scope of application. The global population is projected to grow more and more, reaching 9 billions by the year 2050, so IoT devices are needed in agriculture to increase crop yield and therefore feed sources. However, this solution is not exempt from challenges. Weather conditions, climate change and the environment have a great impact on farming practices. To reduce the costs and losses involved in these activities, we analyze the use of the equipment provided by Adcon Telemetry, such as solutions for plant monitoring, disease detection, frost warning, decision support, management and water quality. All data collected by Adcon equipment can be viewed on the addVANTAGE Pro platform, which can be accessed anywhere using a web browser and Internet connection, in graphical or tabular form.

articleTitle: Dynamic Simulation of a Stand-Alone Photovoltaic/Battery Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Renewable energy is extensively used as primary energy source, in order to meet environmental constraints in a continuously increasing electricity demand framework. This paper presents a model, built in Matlab environment, for a standalone system consisting of a PV array and an electrochemical storage component. Sizing of the elements aimed capturing all the energy generated by the PV panels and being able to meet the load at any time, still considering technical-economic aspects. After having established the general outline, the system was modeled using Simscape/SimpowerSystems blocks to observe the dynamic interaction between the generating component, the storage one and the load. Four types of batteries were used and differences concerning dynamic behavior were discussed.

articleTitle: Using Frequency measurements for data consistency assessment related to malicious data injection in distribution related ICT systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The new active distribution grids ask for ICT systems to support the grid observability and control. However, Information and Communication systems are prone to cyber attacks and high effort is focused on detection of cyber attacks which may bring malicious data injection in the control systems. The paper shows how frequency, as a common parameter in the synchronous power systems, can be used to assess data consistency over the grid, thus being able to detect eventual intrusions through cyber-attacks, by analyzing in real-time its evolution at different levels in the grid (on-line) or by making off-line assessments on recorded data. Selected examples and their interpretations are given in the paper, to show the effectiveness of the method. Moreover, detection of grid faults has been also shown to be possible by using the same tools based on frequency measurement over the grid.

articleTitle: Effect of Iron and Aluminum Powders on the Properties of Composites with Isotactic Polypropylene
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: It is studied the behavior of composite materials with isotactic polypropylene (iPP) matrix and iron (Fe) and aluminum (Al) metallic powders. Concentrations of metallic powders were 3, 5 and 8 %. The raw materials are mixed in a turbula in the required quantities and the melt is injected in the form of the samples used in the measurements. The Al and Fe powders had two granulations. A comparative study is made in the case of materials for the mechanical, thermal and electrical characteristics. Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) and Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) measurements allowed to explain the changes in the structure.

articleTitle: High Precision Test System for the Investigation of the Condition of Lithium-ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Modern electric drive systems require more sophisticated monitoring and diagnosis methods for determining the expected life-time and reliability. Recently, continuous assessment of the electrical condition of electrical machines has become increasingly important. Investigations to predict battery life are of the utmost importance for Electric Vehicles (EVs). The evaluation of the instantaneous State-of-Health (SoH) of the battery cell packs requires a precise measurement system that encompasses the especially important specifications related to the operating conditions. In addition modern Battery Management Systems (BMS) rely on empirical battery models whose parametrization is crucial from the reliability's point of view. The model parameters are necessary to be indentified via the appropriate measurement data. To address these considerations, this paper presents a new test system for Li-ion batteries and control software based on LabView, which is capable of conducting high quality and completely automated battery cell measurements defined by user input test vectors and test suites. The test system allows conducting also real time condition monitoring in Li-ion batteries by discharge impulse responses. Finally several measurements on the experimental setup are performed. Analysis of the measured data validate that the designed device ensures high performance testing and post-processing.

articleTitle: Testing of two Thermographic Devices with two types of Temperature Sensors for Detecting and Locating of Incipient Breast Tumors
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In this paper we present the challenges that arise in using devices based on contact thermography that are to be used for the detection and localization of very early breast cancers. Both devices can be connected to a PC using the common USB port. Two types of temperature sensors arrays are used: a junction diode array and a NTC resistor array. The breast temperature is sampled at a number of points with the sensor array. The data from the sensor array is used to obtain the difference and normalized fields which are then interpolated over the full breast surface. Disturbances in these fields could indicate the presence of a tumor. This interpolated field is part of the boundary condition for the Pennes equation and could be used to locate the tumor by solving an inverse temperature field problem.

articleTitle: Evaluation of PV Panels by a Spline - Fuzzy Approximation and Classification Method
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In this paper is proposed a method for assessment of PV panels by a computational method developed of approximation and classification. The assessment of PV panels is made on the large area of imposed condition existing in operation. On the first level of assessment is taking into account the variation of current and voltage on the terminals of PV panels. At the second level is tacked the dust influence on the output power of PV panels. This general method allows the extending of evaluation in a multi-dimensional space, where all the current techniques has a slight accurateness. The developed method is a general one and may be successful applied for all the types of PV panels with the help only on a small amount of data.

articleTitle: Impact of Steinmetz Coefficients Variance for FeSi Laminate Magnetic Cores
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: An experimental study on the magnetic losses estimation by Steinmetz formulas for non-oriented grains FeSi laminated cores is analyzed. The influence of the involved measured data on the Steinmetz coefficients is presented, detailing the impact of the fitted parameters on the estimated magnetic losses. The experimental setup uses a laminated ring with primary and secondary coils, connected to a commercial permeameter, the measurements including hysteresis cycles for various amplitudes (up to 1.3 T) and frequencies (up to 300 Hz). Two analytical losses formulas are used: the classical Steinmetz model and the generalized formula involving losses separation. The study shows the major impact of the coefficients variance on the losses estimation accuracy, especially for higher frequencies.

articleTitle: Weighting and Classification of Image Features using Optimization Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In this study, importance ratios of features extracted from images using feature extraction algorithms are examined. A significance coefficient is determined for each feature parameter. The number of features is reduced according to the weight of the importance calculated for each feature. The classification success is examined for each case. Firstly, six feature extraction algorithms are used for this purpose. The classification success of all these feature extraction algorithms has been examined separately. Then, all properties are combined to form a single property matrix. The obtained property matrix is reduced by using principal component analysis and relieff methods. New feature matrices provide increased classification performance. However, it is inefficient to classify a high number of properties in real-time applications. To overcome this problem, the effect of classifying each parameter in the property matrix is examined and the insignificant properties are discarded. The proposed method is tested using histopathological images. Histopathological images are divided into 4 separate classes. The proposed method reduces the raw feature matrix by 50% with 97.2% classification success.

articleTitle: Estimation of the Damaged Zone Width due to Mechanical Cutting on High Quality Non-Oriented Steels
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In electrical machine production, the mechanical cutting procedure induces plastic deformation and mechanical stresses, which are directly linked to the magnetic properties' degradation. In spite that the non-oriented electrical steel has a small magnetocrystalline anisotropy, the influence of the easy and hard magnetization axes on the magnetic permeability and energy losses is important. In this study we present a mathematical model, used for the damaged zone width estimation that results from the mechanical punching procedure. Through this technological cutting method NO20 non-oriented electrical steel strips of 300 mm × 30 mm were prepared, being cut parallel (RD) and normal (TD) to the rolling direction. The Epstein standard sample 30 mm in width was reconstructed, by putting together strips having their width in an interval between 5 mm and 30 mm. These samples were assessed utilizing a laboratory Single Strip Tester (SST) for frequency ranging from 3 Hz to 400 Hz, at J<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> = 1 T (peak magnetic polarization value). Using the statistical theory of losses (STL) total energy losses were decomposed into hysteresis, classical and excess losses, and their variation was investigated as a dependence of the strip width.

articleTitle: Automatic control system for stage lights
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In this paper we present an automatic control system for stage lights that can be used for small events. The system has two main functions: it can perform a generic light show that corresponds to a specific music type like jazz, pop or rock, or it can adapt to the music performed on stage by the artist. The system uses an Arduino Mega for processing the collected data from a MEMS microphone breakout board and a specialized graphic equalizer chip and for controlling the LED lights. The system is designed to be in the low cost range so an independent or debutant artist can acquire it.

articleTitle: Designing and Testing of a Low Current Active Band Stop Filter
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The paper presents aspects concerning the designing, simulation and testing of a low current active band stop filter. The filter is realized with two low pass and high pass filter cells connected in parallel. The operational amplifiers using in the designing stage are TL084. Based on the RC elements' values and on the simulated frequency characteristics using a dedicated software, the proposed filter was realized. Finally the results obtained by simulation are validated through experimental ones.

articleTitle: Calculating the power of the electric motor for a single stage turbo blower
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The paper presents the computation methodology for the optimum dimensioning of the necessary power for the driving motor of a turbo blower, depending on the requirements of the industrial process. The turbo blowers are high-speed pneumatic bladed machines, used for raising the pressure of gas. The turbo blower can be driven with a three-phase asynchronous motor or with a gas engine turbine. The power engine computation program for the turbo blower was realized in Mathcad. The present paper adds novelty by the 3D graphic analysis for the dimensioning of a driving motor of a turbo blower through the program elaborated.

articleTitle: Universal DC Motor Protection System Based on Microcontroller Embedded Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: One of the industrial challenges for verifying, analyzing and controlling aggregates powered by DC motors is to provide protection against variations beyond the nominal operating limits of these machines, which makes it opportune to study and test a digital system able to cope with the requirements analysis and control at a low cost, easy to deploy and use. The present paper proposes an optimized technical solution for a wide range of continuous current motors to achieve low voltage, overvoltage and overload protection. A circuit driven by a microcontroller is used which, based on the information acquired from the sensors, will protect the motor by means of a relay.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Performances in Lossless Data Compression for English and Romanian Text Files Using the Q-Coder
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In order to achieve the best and most relevant performance in the field of lossless data compression, but also in order to deepen and refine the results obtained by the type of data to which the compression and decompression operation is applied, this work focuses on compression using the Q-coder, which is a relatively new and less-used coder than the QM-coder, which largely uses the same principles, except that the QM -coder is better known, being mainly used in the JPEG standard. Based on coding and decoding principles using the Q-Coder, its compression performances are compared with other similar compression methods, techniques and algorithms by applying compression to text files in both English and Romanian languages but also on other types of data (images) that allow efficient storage of information in the memory of desktop, mobile or portable computing systems. The experimental results obtained for the compression performance differ significantly depending on the inner characteristics and statistical particularities of each studied natural language. The article interprets these comparative tests and highlights the subsequent differences in compression performance, providing useful conclusions and recommendations, which can be extended to texts from different other natural languages.

articleTitle: Influence of the Air Gap of Hybrid Systems with Magnetic Flux Modulation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Influence of air gap in the main magnetic path is studied in a hybrid system with magnetic flux modulation. The constant magnetic flux is generated by permanent magnets and additional magnetic field is applied to the system by externally power supplied coils.

articleTitle: 100 Years - Evolution of Electrical Engineering Curriculum
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The evolution of the society towards an economy that is based on knowledge and information determines a new definition of electrical engineering. In this paper, it is considered a different approach regarding the electrical energy systems as power systems that are controlled with the use of microprocessors, taking as reference the situation from 100 years ago. New tendencies that can be found in the reform of electrical engineering curricula are discussed and also some invariants.

articleTitle: A new method of estimating the maximum power point coordinates for PV cells, the intersection method
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In this paper is presented a new method for accurately identifying the coordinates of the maximum power point on the IV curve. Based on the presented method are identified a set of analytical equations used for the evaluation of the coordinates of the maximum power point. The presented analytical relations ensure, under certain conditions, determination of the maximum power with a better accuracy of 1%. The maximum power point is evaluated based on a point at the intersection between a special line (d) and the I-V characteristic curve. Determination of the analytical relations is based on the explicit form of the I-V characteristic expressed with Lambert W-function.

articleTitle: Energy Consumption Forecasting to Small and Medium Enterprises Using a Hybrid Method
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In the paper, a hybrid method based on the linear regression model improved with clustering techniques is proposed for the electricity consumption forecasting to Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs). The method has as its starting point the dependence between electricity consumption and climatic factors (temperature, humidity and wind speed). The testing was made considering the case of a small enterprise and the obtained results led at smaller forecasting errors than in the case of using the simple linear regression method, with the average error in the analysed period (a week) by 2.72 % compared to 4.44 %.

articleTitle: Improved Pareto Chart Analysis for Yield Detractors’ Identification
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Nowadays integrated circuits (ICs) are produced in very fine technologies and include increasingly complex functions demanded by the new industry trends. This makes them even more sensitive to process variations than before. Variation is an expensive problem which can cause product delays, yield loss and redesign. Therefore, methods are needed for a quick and accurate IC yield analysis and failure root cause discovery in a cost- and time-efficient way. The paper introduces an improvement of the current Pareto chart analysis employed for yield detractors' identification using data-driven methods. This is achieved by performing clustering prior to the Pareto chart analysis. It proved to be a simpler method, which also leads to the identification of the yield detractors in reduced time compared to the classical Pareto chart analysis..

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Nanoparticles Dispersion for the Realization of ACFs
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The main innovation target is to develop a world leading manufacturing process for continuous production of unique Anisotropic Conductive Films (ACF).

articleTitle: Power Loss Reduction of Discontinuous PWM in Two-Level Voltage Source Converters
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This paper presents a comparison between Space Vector PWM and Discontinuous PWM with clamping to the negative supply, in terms of power losses of the transistors and diodes in an inverter for AC motor drives. The proposed approach used for the power loss estimation uses an advanced method based on power loss models that are evaluated at each simulation step. The power losses are compared based on results from several simulations using a three-phase inverter with a RL load or three current sources so that the power factor can be controlled. The two modulation methods are used one at a time to measure the power loss in the inverter, the phase voltage and the phase current with its maximum. Based on the simulation results, a comparison between the power loss in the two cases is made, depending on the power factor and the amplitude of the output current.

articleTitle: Secured Monitoring of an Automated Parking Building System
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: It is described a system for automated parking building system. The status of the parking building refers to temperature, humidity, presence of combustion gases, and number of available parking places. This information is available both locally using a display and remotely using the internet service. As the monitoring data describing the status of the parking system is sensitive information that can be exploited in a destructive way by non-moderate groups. To alleviate this issue an encryption algorithm has been developed. The originality consists in the seed key code generation technique that is time dependent and more over it is not transmitted through the communication channel between the transmitter and the receiver.

articleTitle: A Project Oriented Laboratory of Embedded Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This paper presents a laboratory of Embedded Control Systems, for the Electrical Engineering students. The laboratory is project oriented, whose final goal is to develop a complete platform of motion control, with well-defined specification, including simple mechanics and quite complex drive system, consisting in motor and motion control, making use of feedback sensors. Our desire, sustained by many studies proving the benefits of "learning-by-doing" approach, is to motivate the students to rapidly acquire/recall knowledge and develop skills, mainly related to electronics and software design and implementation, having a clear image of what and why they are doing in order to complete every project stage. Moreover, we gave an equal importance to make the students learn and work with "the big picture" in mind - the system purpose, its functionality and related knowledge, all perceived and integrated as a whole, with the motivation to "make it work". The project includes hardware development, simulation, software design and implementation, and finally testing. This paper details the project stages, emphasizing the students' activities, and it presents some relevant results.

articleTitle: Contributions in Modern Electrical Engineering Higher Education Using Dedicated Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This paper deals with some of our contributions in developing and using dedicated software in the educational process. We present some simple virtual instruments and Flash applications we made that are useful in teaching and learning activities. All of these applications were developed with and for the students being helpful for them to better understand the electric circuits and systems behavior under different operating conditions.

articleTitle: Voltage and current performance of a three-phase transformer under unbalanced voltage supply
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the voltage unbalance effects in a three-phase transformer for voltage and currents in the secondary side when an unbalanced voltage appears in the primary side. Theory about the voltage unbalance characterization and the unbalance factors is presented. Also, a description of the three-phase transformer selected for the research is showed, together with its model and the equivalent circuit used in the simulations. Clear linear trends are observed between the voltage and current unbalance factors of the primary and secondary side of the transformer, which allows to estimate the performance of the transformer under different voltage unbalance cases. A certain voltage unbalance in the primary side produces an unbalance of voltages and currents in the secondary side, regardless the load index of the transformer.

articleTitle: Concerning the separation of space charge at the DC cable joints interfaces
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This paper presents a study concerning the experimental and theoretical determination of the charge separated at the EPR/XLPE joint interface.Taking into consideration the values of the electrical conductivities and permittivities experimentally determined, the relaxation times of the electric charge, charge density s separated at the interface EPR/XLPE and those of the electric field were computed, both in electrostatic and steady-state regimes.It has been found that the computed values of s are close to those determined experimentally, that s increases in time and with temperature. The higher values of s lead to the intensification of the electric field during the operation and of the residual electric field after power-off.

articleTitle: Aspects of Fractional Calculus in RLC Circuits
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This paper deals with applications of fractional calculus to electrical circuits, a special attention being given to RLC circuits. The main purpose of this paper is to determine and discuss the solution of the fractional RLC series circuit model in the form of a fractional integro-differential equation. The fractional solution obtained is analyzed comparing it with the solution obtained by other computational methods already studied.

articleTitle: A Compact Experimental Device for the Study of Transient Mode in Electrical Circuits
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Higher technical education has as its primary objective the transmission of theoretical knowledge of specialty but also practical activities whereby students acquire the habits and practical skills necessary for future engineering careers. The acquisition of practical abilities takes place during the laboratory classes during which the students have the opportunity to make experimental installations, to work with modern technical equipment, to collect and interpret experimental data. In this paper is presented a compact didactic use equipment designed for studying the transient mode in electrical circuits (charging/discharging of a capacitor, a R, L, C circuit operating powered by a rectangular signal source) realized on modern pedagogical principles that comes in support of students from the Faculty of Electrical Engineering in Craiova. Validation of the experimental device dimensioning accuracy was achieved by comparing the results obtained using the new experimental platform with the results obtained by computerized modeling using dedicated software.

articleTitle: Analysis of energy efficient solutions for electric transportation of smart cities
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In this paper we analyzed the brake energy recovery solution as well as the energy use solutions for powering an advanced tram station. We have also identified an additional technical solution for mobile electrical storage, placed at the end of the tram line. The research effort was directed in two main ways. First was identifying the receiver assembly and the functionality of the modern tram station and modeling its operating cycles. The solution was subjected to an economic analysis to identify the feasibility of implementing this solution in a smart city. The second was to identify the optimal brake energy recovery solution as well as the energy efficiency of this technology chain. This approach was supported by a team of engineers from RATB, with whom we kept constant contact and validated (or invalidated) the various technical solutions originally proposed.

articleTitle: Experimental model of thermoelectric power plant with gamma Stirling engine
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Increasing environmental pollution by using fossil fuels to obtain electricity requires the replacement of these renewable energies with renewable energy. One of the renewable energies is the solar one. Solar energy can be used to generate electricity using photovoltaic cells, respectively with Stirling engine and Fresnel lenses. Using Fresnel lenses, the solar radiation is concentrated on the engines warm area, increasing the temperature of that area. In this paper we analyze an experimental model of the thermoelectric power plant where the solar radiation is replaced by the energy obtained by burning butane. A butane lamp is used for this. It is analyzed how different parameters influence the functioning of the thermoelectric power plant. The Stirling engine used is of gamma type and the electric generator is DC. It is studied how the value of the load resistance and generator speed influences the power plants efficiency. It is also studied how the temperature value of the hot zone or cold area influences the efficiency of the Stirling engine and how the efficiency of the experimental model of the thermoelectric power plant is influenced by the value of the generator load resistance, the temperature of the hot zone and the cold area of the Stirling engine, and the speed of the electric generator.

articleTitle: Improved Fault Ride-Through Strategy for DWIG in Wind Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This paper proposes a complementary system for Dual Stator Winding Induction Generator (DWIG) in Wind Power Applications. This additional system improves the Low- Voltage Ride-Through capability of this kind of generator. This paper introduces a technique to avoid the overrating current, assuring the protection of the Control-Winding Side Converter, by means of adding a dynamic crowbar to the wind power system. In addition, the solution presented here can be used also to regulate the power in a hybrid micro-grid, with both DC, and AC distribution, increasing also its ride-through capability. Therefore, the proposed strategy helps to integrate the microgrid components, sources and loads, in the electrical grid.

articleTitle: On Optimization of Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The main objective of this paper is a study with reference to the optimal electromagnetic power wireless transfer, and with direct application on battery chargers. The main elements impacting the optimal operation of the wireless battery charging systems are: load resistance, mutual coupling factor and the parameters of secondary coil. It is assumed that the two magnetically coupled coils operate at the same resonance frequency, which has a common value for both circuits, source and receiver. The mode the two coils are connected, influences the values of the optimum efficiency and maximum amount of active power transferred to the load, with the best results for the "series-series" connection. The magnetically coupled systems must be able to ensure a fast and reliable charging of ultra-capacitors used for the storage of energy. Whereas charging the ultra-capacitors is a fast process, the standard inductively coupled circuits can deliver maximum power only if the impedance of the load reaches a well determined value. This value strongly depends on the shape and dimensions of each coil, as well as the space between the coils. The impedance of the load must be brought to an optimum value, according to the request for optimum efficiency in conditions maximum active power transfer. The procedure involves inductivity adjustment for the secondary coil, accompanied by determination of tuning capacitance at resonance. Optimal efficiency value and maximum real power transferred to the load have been determined through parameter analysis.

articleTitle: Ultra low current measurement system for nuclear applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This work is focused on the design of a measurement platform intended to be used for very low current measurements in a particle accelerator facility. The existing system of the accelerator allows the particle beam current measurement in microamperes range with a resolution of 100nA. The platform is attached to the accelerator existing system to quantify ultra low current values currents measurements, which extends the range up to values of the order of the picoampers. Certain aspects like the influence of the external low frequency noise and a proper electromagnetic shielding are considered to reduce the noise of the system.

articleTitle: Magnetostatic Analysis of SRM Supported by Hybrid FEM-ANN Method
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In this article the hybrid method combining the FEM with artificial neural network is depicted. The goal of the method is to obtain the magnetostatic characteristics of the switched reluctance motor. The method focuses on maximal computation time reduction and simultaneously on keeping the solution accuracy. The model of the artificial neural network is based on reduced FEM simulation. For neural network training and testing selected data from FEM simulation were applied. The model of ANN was used to obtain full magnetostatic characteristics of the SRM. Comparison with numerical magnetic field solver proved the hybrid model reliability. To create the ANN model we applied APLAC programming language and embedded libraries of this software, for FEM simulation we used the FEMM tool. The novelty of the paper is the code, which automates date transfer between APLAC and FEMM software. With the use of the hybrid FEM-ANN method we obtained significant accelerations of the field computations.

articleTitle: Algorithms and Control Structures for Photovoltaic Modules Installed on Large Transportation Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Can the sun radiation replace internal combustion fuels? If we take into account recent technology evolutions, the answer is certainly yes-at least in some applications. Photovoltaic modules have become a lot cheaper lately and this makes them extremely attractive for the transportation market. Integrating photovoltaics into transportation vehicles contributes to lower fuel consumption and CO2 emissions, as well as reduced costs. The main purpose of this paper consist in proposing a viable way of integrating photovoltaics into truck trailers, with respect to efficiency, cost reduction and optimization of the hole process. We propose a series of algorithms and control structures for the PV micro-grids, which can cope better with specific disturbances and offer better predictability. The PV grid is divided into subgroups of optimal dimensions chosen after applying certain strategies and an optimization algorithm.

articleTitle: A new Multiple Input Multiple Output V2V automotive antenna for Long Term Evolution band applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to evaluate a dual-band Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output (MIMO) Long Term Evolution (LTE) antenna for automotive applications. Such an antenna has an overall volume relatively small and can be fit in different locations on the vehicle. The compact planar structure facilitates that. The antenna is composed of two radiant symmetrical elements connected through a neutralizing line in order to cancel the reactive coupling. The radiating element consisting of a folded monopole and a rectangular metal patch can produce multiple resonant modes at 800 MHz (790-862 MHz) and 2600 MHz (2575-2635 MHz) for the geographical region of Europe. The proposed antenna is fed by using 50 Ω coplanar waveguide (CPW) transmission lines.

articleTitle: Voltage control in low voltage campus distribution with high PV penetration
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Over the last years, the PV systems have become a very attractive solution in view of achieving sustainability and efficient local generation with applicability for university campuses. However, such grids exhibit high load variation spanning from low (during vacation) to high (during winter semesters, for example). Thus, the voltage regulation in low voltage grids becomes important. The purpose of this work is to present five control strategies for voltage regulation based either on using electricity storage, transformer tap changing or on a combination of both.

articleTitle: Half-split Dielectric Resonator Antennas Using High-Dielectric Permittivity Barium Neodymium Titanate
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Barium neodymium titanate material was manufactured by using solid-state reaction technique. Two types of microstrip fed antennas using half-split cylindrical resonators of barium neodymium titanate are proposed. New methods for coupling modes are investigated in order to increase the impedance bandwidth. For the 2.4 GHz band antenna, a 174 MHz impedance bandwidth was obtained, which is a very good value for a resonator of dielectric constant greater than 84. Due to the high dielectric constant, the volume of the used resonator is less than a sixth of previously reported dielectric resonator, which makes the antennas more compact and cost-effective.

articleTitle: Using Real-Time Spectrum Analyzer for EMC Near-Field Measurements and EMC Education
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Real-time spectrum analyzer is a very useful novel measurement equipment for EMC troubleshooting and EMC educational purposes. In this paper is presented some basics and benefits of the real-time spectrum analyzers. In empirical part it is used two demoboards for measuring and demonstrating the effectiveness of the real-time spectrum analyzer in magnetic near-field measurement for EMC troubleshooting. This kind of demonstration measurement can be directly applied for the EMC educational purposes. The real-time spectrum analyzer is also very useful equipment for different wireless IoT device measurements.

articleTitle: Prescribing the electric power at wind power systems, based on variable weather conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The present paper determines the electric power for a wind power system, according to the time varying wind speed, v. The wind power system (WPS) consists of a wind turbine, WT and a synchronous generator with permanent magnets, SGPM. The electrical power becomes a prescribed value, P*, of the control system, ensuring stable operation and maximum captured wind power. Operation at the maximum power point (MPP) at the optimal mechanical angular speed (MAS), ω<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OPTIM</sub>, in the conditions in those the wind speed decreases over time causes transition to an unstable area, MAS decreasing over time. For this reason, in present, at stable operation of the wind power system, the MAS values are higher than ω<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OPTIM</sub>. The prescribed power values, P<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>, are calculated in such a way that the WPS should operate stable and the captured wind power is as high as possible. To determine the prescribed power value, an algorithm is proposed that considers rapid wind speed variations. Measuring the basic functional sizes, MAS and the electric debt energy by the SGPM, we determine the dependence of optimal MAS to the wind speed and bring the WPS in the optimal operation area by modifying the generators load.

articleTitle: Reduction of the Distributed Electric Energy - A Challenge for the Distribution Operators Case Study - Arcelor Mittal Galati
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The paper highlights the risk for distribution operators from decreasing the amount of distributed energy point of view, as a result of transformations in the energy market or the disappearance of a customer for which significant volumes of installations were made including the expenses related to their maintenance. From its impact point of view on income, by reducing the amount of billable electricity through the application of distribution tariffs is a risk that the main distribution operators have to take into account. The existence of a history of unfavourable regulatory conditions for operators as well as an insufficient degree of transparency in the setting of distribution tariffs leads to a particularly serious risk for distribution operators. The emergence of decentralized production units greatly alters the costs of distribution activity, costs that are only highlighted for distributed (consumed) electricity. In a certain context ARCELOR MITTAL Galati convinced the decision makers that they can give up to the existing power distribution network by making parallel connections and keeping in reserve some of the installations that will connect with the National Power System without transit of energy just from safety reasons. If the distribution service billing is made only at the level of the electricity consumption, as the network costs are both fixed and variable, the distribution operators are disadvantaged. In addition, the methodologies for calculating distribution tariffs must also reflect the support that should be given to the research activities related to this field. Starting from the presented case study, different analysis assumptions can be made at the level of each distribution operator, as well as at each voltage level.

articleTitle: Printed Monopole Arrowhead Antenna Compared to Microstrip Rectangular Antenna on High Dielectric Constant Substrate
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: A microstrip and a printed monopole antenna were designed for 5.8 GHz frequency band on the same 0.5 mm thick high dielectric constant substrate. For printed monopole antenna, a new arrowhead antenna is proposed. The arrowhead monopole antenna exhibit a 2.75 GHz impedance bandwidth, much larger than the 30 MHz bandwidth of the microstrip rectangular antenna. However, the antenna patterns show that the arrowhead monopole antenna exhibit lower directivity than the rectangular microstrip antenna.

articleTitle: Wireless Sensors Network based on Real-time Healthcare Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Healthcare surveillance systems based on the wireless sensors network have developed a large scale increase in the recent years. These systems are more important to human life and provide the appropriate techniques to be applied. The proposed healthcare monitoring system is designed based on the wireless sensors network. The system senses and displays the electrocardiogram, blood oxygen saturation, heart rate, and patient temperature in real-time. Vital indicators are extracted from the patient's body by sensors. In case of a critical situation, the vital signs are sent to a specialist doctor.

articleTitle: An Integrated Probabilistic Approach for Power Transformers Availability
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The paper present an integrated approach of power transformers availability considering 7 high power 110/6.3 kV and 20 years as the monitoring time interval. With respect to a given load point, the interruptions frequency, duration and cause are revealed on a statistical bases. Not only the PTs and their unavailability but also the surround equipment like circuit-breakers, feeder and load point events were included as interruption sources. For PTs, internal and external failures as well as the planned (maintenance) events were considered.Time to failure, time to repair, mean time between events and its progress over time were probabilistically estimated. The results allow for a better maintenance management and for a good estimation of the quality of supply.

articleTitle: Propensity of enroling in Electrical and Power Engineering. Case study of Technical University of Cluj-Napoca
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The main task of higher education in engineering is to provide for students a specific set of knowledge, skills and attitudes to be able applying them in conceiving, designing, implementing, and operating systems, products, processes and projects. Therefore, students, as future engineers, must be technical, on the one hand, but socially responsible and eager to innovate, on the other hand. Moreover, it is well known that engineering is perceived as the driver of innovation along with economic development. An effectively, innovating and applied engineering can be the determinant factor even for the poverty reduction, sustainable development and climate change. In this context, the present article aims at identifying the propensity of candidates’ form Transylvania region of Romania for Electrical and Power Engineering Education. An overview on some related factors of the economic environment is provided focused on specific opportunities and threats of the engineering hiring market analyses. The global, European and local situation have been considered. The study case on Technical University of Cluj-Napoca insists on particularities of Electrical and Power Engineering admission issues. The analyze of admission candidate’s evolution since 2012 display an increasing attraction to the electrical engineering domain.

Author Keywords: Electrical and Power Engineering education; job opporunities

articleTitle: Records of Failures to Railroad Safety Installation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: To have a more comprehensive overview of failures to railroad traffic installations, the installations must be monitored permanently. In this work we propose a record software that allows a rapid identification of the train stations with the most failures, their causes, of the installations with the most number of failures, and so on. Based on the data shown by the software, coercive measures can be taken to improve the quality of the maintenance work, or to detect the weak components. The software we present in this work can be used at the (Romanian) national level and graphically shows the monitoring results.

articleTitle: Non-invasive Acquisition of Bio-potentials for ECG
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This paper proposes a bio-potential measurement solution for the acquisition of electrocardiogram, by a system based on the USB-6218 acquisition board made by National Instruments. Information will be acquired in a non-invasive way through several electrodes applied to the human body at specific points. The bio-potentials will be taken and sent via the electrodes and connectors to the USB-6218 acquisition board. Implementation of the system is done without any external hardware amplification or filtering hardware. Data acquisition and processing have been done through the development platform and environment called LabVIEW using graphical code. After the development and implementation of the virtual acquisition and processing tools, a control and display panel has been developed, playing the role of user interface. Several subjects of different age, height, body mass, and sexes have been evaluated within this work, in order to observe a wide range of waveforms and significant signal parameters. The obtained results will be stored in a local database on the device that USB-6218 acquisition board will be connected to.

articleTitle: Selection of the Main Parameters for Long Term Prediction of the Atmospheric Boundary Layer in Romanian Wind Farms
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Romania has the highest wind potential from Southeast Europe, representing nowadays more than 14,000 MW. In January 2017, in Romania have been registered 3025 MW produced energy by the wind power farms, representing investments over 5 billion euros. It represents more than 24% of the total delivered electric energy. The analyzed area presented in this paper is located in the south part of Moldavia, being considered until the altitude of 600 m. Firstly a database was realized of the main measured parameters with three masts, situated at approx 20 km distance each other. Around ten parameters of the main environmental data, for more than one year, were registered and completed with measurements from other five meteorological stations. Based on this database, the initial conditions for numerical modeling of the vertical wind distribution were established. In the beginning, some theoretical aspects concerning the influence of the Boundary Layer separation on air velocity distribution are mentioned. For this domain an altimetry model was established. At the beginning, an average value of roughness was considered. As a second step for modeling, based on the local conditions, the effective roughness was estimated and some corrections were made. In these conditions supplementary parameters are necessary to evaluate the turbulence. The air density, pressure, and temperature, also registered, have an essential role in the proper evaluation of the wind velocity. It represents the principal factor affecting the functioning of the wind turbines. The numerical model takes into account the database of the measured parameters and the corrections made due to the variable roughness. It is established a Long Term Prediction for the vertical distribution of the air velocity, and was estimated the wind farm efficiency. Finally, some numerical results, conclusions, and references are presented.

articleTitle: Healthcare System Based on the Smart Monitoring Bracelets and Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Electronic healthcare devices are considerably more utilized as the time passes. Pregnant women who suffer from preeclampsia and the persons who have cardiac diseases can have their heart rate monitored through the use of a smart bracelet. The created bracelet sends the measured values towards the user's associated smart phone and then to the system's server. The server interprets the health parameters and alerts the associated relatives, caregivers and the doctor in case of an emergency by sending an SMS. On the system's forum the bracelet's user can write about the current health symptoms and the medical experience. Sentiment analysis is applied to determine if a critical situation has been described. In this case, an SMS alert is delivered to the user's doctor. This close connection between the patient and doctor upgrades the quality of life.

articleTitle: Smart metering deployment status across EU-28
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: The scope of this paper is to present an EU-28 overview of the smart meter roll-out implementation progress. The study is based on publicly available information and presents a traffic light map with the deployment status by mid-2017. A series of particular cases are approached and a gap between the European Commission recommendation, expected diffusion rate and actual deployment is identified. The study further provides some possible causes considering the number of metering points available at EU-28 level, country specific assumed targets and macro-environmental factors.

articleTitle: An Overview of the Properties and Industrial Applications of Shape Memory Alloys
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In shape memory alloys (SMAs), the thermoelastic martensitic transformation between austenite and martensite phases leads to the appearance of the shape memory effect and super-elasticity. In addition, these alloys present high mechanical strength, great ductility, vibration damping property and hysteresis behavior. All of the above-mentioned properties make these alloys very promising for industrial applications and their usage leads to the increase of productivity and efficiency of the devices they pertain to. The purpose of this article is, on the one hand, to increase the awareness of R & D engineers about the existence and use of SMAs by describing and promoting the unusual properties and effects of these materials and, on the other hand, to outline some of their most promising industrial applications.

articleTitle: Enabling smart monitoring applications for mobile military hospital using wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN) based applications that give smart capabilities to homes, warehouses, factories, farms, power grids, are becoming more popular than ever. In this short paper we presenting a series of hardware and software solutions integrated into a novel infrastructure that gives smart capabilities to a more unusual target - a NATO role 2E mobile military hospital. Our work is motivated by our own analysis of such a medical facility deployed for a training exercise. In addition to traditional logistics problems, several specific requirements have been defined in order to help motivate and define our complex WSN based infrastructure. The proposed solutions are based on off-the-shelf hardware components and freely available supported software components.

articleTitle: Parametric macromodels for the RF behaviour of capacitive switches
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: This article proposes a new methodology dedicated to the extraction of RF parametric macro-models for electrostatically actuated micro switches. The sensitivities of the geometric parameters of the macro-model's components are calculated and inserted into a parametric RF macro-model. The extraction algorithm uses the results obtained from three RF simulations performed on the field model of the device. The solving of the numerical problem was performed with the finite integrals technique and using a closed form fitting procedure for the TL-lumped macro-model. A procedure that calculates the sensitivity of the RF output with respect to the parameter that varies is included in a finite integration technique in-house code. The methodology is validated for a capacitive switch from the literature.

articleTitle: Resilience through Self-Sufficiency in Smart Cities: A Preliminary Bucharest Use Case
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Cities follow new trends towards extreme social and technological development. The Smart City concept includes many innovative aspects, but an essential one is the capability to generate its own clean energy, leading to an increased energy resilience and immunity against major disturbances, as a mitigation of the negative impact of global warming related extreme weather, but also of other blackout inducing events, such as cyber-attacks or evolving faults. The paper presents an assessment for both clean energy production using PVs and resilience, applied for Bucharest city and its neighbour zone Ilfov, showing the conditions for obtaining up to 100% renewable production and high resilience. In this paper, a financial analyse is also performed to check the feasibility of the scenarios, with or without using large storage resources, for achieving different levels of self-sufficiency<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>.

articleTitle: A Review of Methods Used for Revitalizing Books and Reading Experience
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Our paper presents a series of modern ways used for augmenting reading and increasing people's interest in books. In today's society, reading has been replaced with other activities related to technology and the evolution of science. However, the advantages brought in by technology can also be applied to books in order to increase their attractiveness. Virtual and augmented reality, internet of things or movement detection are just a few examples of technologies which can be integrated into classical books and bring with them a great series of advantages: increase interest of young people, raise attractiveness and entertainment. Social collaboration is also an aspect which can help people share their interests, encouraging others to read, write, collaborate, share, thus getting closer to creating a better future of reading. We will also present our current project, Lib2life, which has the purpose of augmenting reading and libraries through interactive 3D reconstructions and social-collaborative means.

articleTitle: Clustering Electrical Retinal Responses Based on Averaged Peri-stimulus Time Histograms
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Visual information is delivered to retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) by the retinal circuit and then transmitted from RGCs to the brain. Among these RGCs, there are over 30 different types and each type carries specialized information about the visual world.
