The question of whether and how RGCs also show different types of responses to electrical stimulation has been much debated for a long time. This work aims to classify RGC responses to pulsed electrical stimulation based on the peri-stimulus time histogram (PSTH). Both hard and soft partitioning methods were used to perform unsupervised clustering. The results of the clustering algorithms were evaluated using cluster validity indices with no prior information. The result was that the k-means as a hard partitioning method provided about 17 clusters, while the fuzzy Gustafson Kessel algorithm gave about 25 clusters. After manual inspection, it was concluded that the clusters are both diverse and specific enough to likely correlate to known RGC types. Therefore, performing clustering based on the electrical pulse-elicited PSTH could be a powerful tool and can contribute in differentiating RGCs and stimulating them selectively.

articleTitle: Microparticle light scattering detection device
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In today's environment microparticles have as sources both natural sources and sources of industrial human activities and not only. There are mixtures of microparticle / air usually known as aerosols and standalone microparticle matter, alone [6]. In the atmosphere exist simultaneously, suspended, these microscopic microparticle, liquid or solid [1] [2]. Human health, due to impacts these microparticle have on environment, climate, precipitation, it is adversely affected. Some of the most dangerous microparticles are soot, amorphous carbon, residue of the incomplete burning of organic matter, ultrafine particles [6], 2.5 μm diameter or less fine particles, between 2.5 and 10 micrometers (μm) diameter which are coarse particles, all being under categories of microparticles that are atmospheric suspended microparticles matter, coarse particles, inhalable particles, thoracic, microparticles that are respirable [1]. Globally, the risk of premature death due to particulate matter microparticles in the ambient environment has been globally ranked 6th in the overall risk of premature death. Due to respiratory infections, lung cancer, chronic pulmonary disease, stroke and heart disease have been recorded worldwide 4.1 million deaths.Microparticles that can and really do penetrate even deeper into the lungs are particularly the most killer microparticles, namely the small ones, increasing by 36% the risk of lung cancer to just 10 μg / m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. In order to be clearly stated, there is no safety or safety level regarding the microparticles, having as proof studies that shows for any increase of 10 μg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, the growth rate in lung cancer increases by 22% [2] [3]. The so-called microparticles suspended in the atmosphere are carcinogenic and represent the most deadly forms of atmospheric air pollution due to their ease and ability to penetrate deep into the lungs into the blood flow without being pre-filtered, thus causing premature death, respiratory diseases, heart attacks, permanent DNA mutations [3].

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling of the Effect produced by repeated floods and estimation of the risk zones
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: In Romania, in the last decades, any plan of management concerning the environmental rehabilitation of the natural riverbeds has not been made. After the floods from 2004, 2005 and 2014 uncontrolled deposits of sediments have been recorded or, in contrary, in other places zones with erosion and uncontrolled coastal slides. As an immediate effect zones with risk for the local population, and not only, have appeared. The present paper estimates the capacity of transport of riverbeds in real conditions, based on local measurements registered during and after the floods. The model is tested for the Bistrita River, an area well-known for repeated floods, sometimes even in the same year. Near the watercourse, there are many locations, with a high population. The time variation of the liquid and solid phases discharged are directly connected with the sediment transport. In these conditions, the fine fractions from the material of the bed sediments are removed from its surface. Some of them become "armored" with the coarser part of the bed sediment. It is proposed a mathematical model to simulate the effect of both types of deposits, to study the surface of an open channel, with a movable bed. The entire alluvial stream, until the base rock, is considered with a small thickness so the non-uniformity of the grain size in vertical distribution from riverbed could be neglected. The boundary conditions in flood analysis consist in the upstream hydrograph and the stationary downstream water level. Knowing the flow rate and the water levels by direct measurements, there is possible to establish the risks zones, far away from the river borders. The primary purpose of this study is to minimize the effects of such uncontrolled floods, to detemine the risk zones and to present a solution for increasing the safety near the riverbed. Finally, some conclusion and references are mentioned.

articleTitle: Velocity and position assessment for robotic arms
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: With the widespread introduction into almost all industries of flexible lines, robotic arms, robots, new problems have emerged that have to be solved [1]. There are in operation right now, perfectly functional and fully equipped, 100% robotized production units without any human operator. In some cases, even operations of maintenance and service are done by robots [1]. An important aspect of this change in the good way of this evolution is the assurance of work safety for human operators involved in industrial activities that involve good and secure cooperation with flexible units, robotic arms, robots [2], [1]. We can work with examples from many industries, such as the medical industry - Da Vinci Surgical System, microelectronics, nanotechnologies, but perhaps the most well-known is the automotive industry [2]. We can give examples belonging of this industry, where robots maneuver much more easily, accurately and efficiently, otherwise difficult to handle automotive components - heavy, such as chassis, car body elements, entire car body and other such items, all out of the possibilities of a human operator. In these intersection situations between flexible units, robotic arms, robots, and human operators, it is obviously necessary to ensure labor protection measures, to incorporate several safe guards to protect human operators against any possible accidents - especially against possible collision situations [3], [2]. At the same time, the software architectures that manages these flexible units, robotic arms, robots, have kept pace with the systems evolution and have made these systems more trustworthy, reliable and to be manage with more ease [3].

articleTitle: Optimization of Storing the Environmental Databases for Future Modeling of Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: To make new investments in power plants based on renewable resources is necessary to perform some pre-feasibility studies. They provide data concerning the energetic capacity of the area. Each review is based firstly on the environmental data monitored for an extended period, at least two years, according to the international rules. These complex databases prove and assure the economic feasibility and future efficiency of the power plants. The paper presents a new solution for recording and storing the environmental measurements, performed during four years with masts having 80 m height. They cover a larger area from the interest zone. Firstly some aspects referring to the mast's characteristic and installation are mentioned. Some observations relating to the influences induced by the masts presence are also briefly illustrated. Elaboration of the database was a challenge, due to the 12 instantly recorded parameters at a time interval of 10 minutes (some of them even at 10 seconds) for four years. Besides these main parameters, some other data were stored, referring to the energy possible to be produced daily, with wind turbines or PV panels. The method of compacting the data is original, to use small amounts of computer memory. With the daily collected values and stored the average, the maximum and minimum values for the wind velocity, temperature, solar radiation, pressure, and humidity were calculated, separately, for each day and month, from the data measured at a time interval of 10 minutes. Some dedicated software was used to realize specific reports referring to the wind farms efficiency, for different classes of wind speed and direction. Another part of the database was structured for extreme values, stored separately. A particular chapter is dedicated to the measurements of the temperature, pressure, humidity and their influence in the solar power plant realization. With the recorded data by numerical modeling a future wind power plant was estimated. Finally, the paper ends with numerical results, some conclusions, and references.

articleTitle: Use Cases and Designs for a Brain-Computer Interface using EEG Wireless Sensors
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering (ISFEE)
abstract: Wireless sensors have developed greatly in the recent years and their applicability spreads to various fields. One that benefited greatly from this development is healthcare. Due to the independence from wires and other specific hardware equipment, these small devices were included in medical equipment with the end goal of aiding specialists in obtaining complete information in a shorter period of time. This led to a decrease in diagnosis time and in an improved success rate for different operations. Desired continuous mobility and poor time management are key factors that led to various brain diseases and not only. To keep pace with this trend, many solutions have been developed over time to counteract this trend and improve the quality of life. Electroencephalography (EEG) sensors have the role to study the activity of the brain in various states and provide measurements that can aid patients and specialists in dealing with certain issues. This paper has the objective to present different use cases in which EEG sensors can be used to detect, diagnose or treat different disorders. Moreover, we have conducted a survey of existing hardware and software solutions that can be integrated with medical sensing hardware. All of these components are meant to be intelligently combined, experimented with and tested for complex healthcare related applications.
